outcome: asset wealth-related inequalities in maternal health outcomes
frequency and timing of prenatal care
cohort: Participants were women in Zimbabwe whose birth timing and maternal health outcomes were captured in nationally representative demographic and health surveys collected between 1999 and 2015.
finding: The RBF programme significantly reduced relative and absolute maternal health inequalities, particularly in prenatal care, caesarean section delivery, and family planning, with more pronounced effects among lower socio-economic groups.
mod_finding: The RBF programme was associated with reductions in disparities for delivery by caesarean section (-0.028, P < 0.005).
